about.title: Auburn Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Auburn sits at a crossroads of commuter and highway traffic, where I-80 funnels through town alongside busy local routes like Grass Valley Highway, Auburn Folsom Road, and Route 49. Placer County's most recent full-year data shows 52 injury collisions and 70 people hurt on Auburn roads, with Friday afternoons between 1 and 3 p.m. seeing more reported crashes than other times. Whether your crash happened merging onto the interstate or waiting at a light on Auburn Folsom Road, the aftermath can mean medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls you didn't ask for. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect people hurt in Auburn crashes with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options. There's no cost to get connected, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. Reaching out early can help make sure evidence from the scene doesn't disappear.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Deadline Is Real
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a county road crew — is involved. Acting sooner rather than later protects your options.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces your payout. What you say in a recorded statement to an insurance adjuster can be used to shift more fault onto you, so it's worth thinking twice before giving one.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic harm in most car accident cases. An attorney can help make sure those losses aren't overlooked or undervalued early in the claims process.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on I-80 near Auburn — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention and document what you can, including photos and any witness information. Try to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company until you've talked to an attorney. Reporting the crash to your own insurer is usually still appropriate, but be cautious about details you volunteer.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only collect a fee if you recover money. There's no upfront cost to you either way.

items.question: Does it matter that my crash happened on Auburn Folsom Road instead of I-80?
items.answer: The road itself doesn't change your legal rights, but jurisdiction and evidence details can differ — for example, whether county maintenance or highway agencies are involved. An attorney can sort through those specifics once you're connected.

items.question: What if the insurance company says the crash was partly my fault?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so even if you're found partially responsible, you can still pursue compensation — it's just reduced by your percentage of fault. Insurers sometimes overstate a driver's fault early on, which is one reason it helps to have someone reviewing the claim on your behalf.
